name: Pampa (Adikavi Pampa)
credit: No contemporary portrait of Pampa is known; the page shows a monogram tile.
bio: Pampa, called Adikavi, the first poet, of Kannada literature, was born in 902 and lived until about 955. He was a Jain by faith, from a family of Brahmin origin that had turned to Jainism, and his family came from the Vengi country; he grew up at Annigeri in what is now Dharwad district of Karnataka. He served at the court of Arikesari II, a Chalukya feudatory ruling at Gangadhara (Vemulavada), who rewarded him with the grant of a village.

He composed two works in the champu form, verse mixed with prose, in the Old Kannada of the tenth century: the Adipurana, on the life of the first Jain Tirthankara, and the Vikramarjuna Vijaya, usually called the Pampa Bharata, both finished in 941. The second retells the Mahabharata with Arjuna as its hero and openly likens him to the poet's patron Arikesari. The twelfth and thirteenth ashvasas (cantos) of that work, which tell of the great battle after the fall of Bhishma, are given here.
